summary.short: Quebec statute amending the public-sector access and privacy Act and the private-sector personal information Act (P-39.1). It sets rules for consent, transparency, privacy impact assessments, incident notification, automated decisions, data releases and penalties for public bodies and enterprises. Most provisions apply from 22 September 2023.
summary.long: The Act amends the Act respecting Access to documents held by public bodies and the Protection of personal information and the Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector, and amends several other statutes, including the Election Act. Public bodies and enterprises must appoint a person in charge of personal information, publish governance rules and policies, and conduct privacy impact assessments for information system projects and before releasing personal information outside Québec. Confidentiality incidents with a risk of serious injury must be reported to the Commission d'accès à l'information and to affected persons. Consent must be clear, free and informed, and express for sensitive information; consent for a minor under 14 is given by a parent or tutor. Persons must be informed of profiling technology and of decisions based exclusively on automated processing, with a right to the reasons and to submit observations. Privacy settings of technological products offered to the public must be set to the highest confidentiality by default. Data may be released for study, research or statistics under a privacy impact assessment and a written agreement. Individuals gain rights to computerized data portability and to de-indexing. Monetary administrative penalties, penal fines and punitive damages are provided, with maxima stated in the Act. Effective dates vary, with most provisions coming into force on 22 September 2023.</br>

notes: Text is the adopted Bill 64 (2021, chapter 25) with explanatory notes, annotated for relations only; quotes are in French with no gloss. target_instrument_id is an empty string for every row because no registry IDs for the targets were supplied; each target is identified by target_text. Commencement (s. 175): most provisions 22 Sept 2023; some 22 Sept 2021 or 22 Sept 2022; s. 30 and part of s. 120 on 22 Sept 2024; s. 160 (new s. 91 of P-39.1) on commencement of s. 108 of the Credit Assessment Agents Act. Internal dependency: new s. 91(3) of P-39.1 refers to s. 8.4, which is created by renumbering in s. 108 of the Credit Assessment Agents Act, not by this Act. Review clauses: s. 73 and s. 157 replace 2011 with 2026 in s. 179 of the Access Act and s. 88 of P-39.1; the text does not state the review content. Repeals inside amended acts are noted under each target. The section_status relations entry is populated only because the schema requires it; relation rows are present.
